attempts.rationale: Ranking is unstable (tau=0.041) and several correlated groups exist; a robust weighted combination with inverse error should capture the best models while being resilient.
Test a robust median combination because ranking is unstable and seasonality is strong; median may reduce influence of outliers.
Test a robust DBA combination to see if iterative search improves over weighted inverse_error, given unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
test a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) to see if a smoother weighting improves over inverse_error while still using all models.
Test a trimmed_mean combination to see if trimming outliers improves over weighted, given unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
try a per‑horizon best‑model weighting to capture changing dominance across the 8‑step horizon in this strongly seasonal, trend‑rich series.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a simple, robust mean may perform comparably to weighted combos.
Try a per‑horizon top‑k mean weighting to capture horizon‑specific model strengths in this highly seasonal series.
The ranking is unstable and several correlated groups exist; a forward selection that builds a diverse pool may capture complementary errors better than simple weighted combos.
Test a weighted combination using the basic inverse_error weighting (w1) to see if simple error‑based weights beat the mean, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.

Try a robust weighted combo on the top‑7 stable models using inverse error weights to see if a focused subset improves over the full‑pool inverse weighting, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality, so a per‑horizon weighted combination on a stable subset may help.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w1' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9995. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.041); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.63.
